change_log: Status: version 2 now replaces version 1 and amendments 2 and 3 only. Amendment 1 stays in force on the owner's word for F1, F2 and the research child's 300k ceiling until he rules (§12).

§1 bullets: the coordinator is labelled low (a 400-character note, harmless because it certifies nothing, Clark-Wilson). The B+ tree governs only the pack at review. The square-root law governs the coordinator and the fresh-review path, and the research child's window is the owner's call. Coverage is held-out seed recall (D8-10), and the completeness estimate is a reading, never a stop or a gate.

§1 table: row 1 now says 'admission by a computed reservation'. Row 3 drops 'LCF kernel' and Gordon/Milner/Wadsworth. Row 6 keeps the B+ tree name, and §7 gets the sentence on what is borrowed at seven leaves (it replaces the old 'Height and B-link buy nothing' sentence, so it is said once).

§4 Borrowed whole: the LCF claim is replaced by: promote.mjs is the only writer of store/status/ (R13), behind the R29 deny rules; only witnessed is certified by a script; confirmed is measured (R42).

Layout: the run root moved out of every repository and every CLAUDE.md/.claude ancestor (example C:/research-runs/2026-11-harness-leads/, its own git repo). run/ now lists coord.json, watcher.json, watcher.lock, run.lock and intents/ (owner messages only). tcb.lock.json is removed from tcb/.

R22 (old R23): the lean baseline comes from a control session in an empty folder outside every repository, and manifests name the user-level files by hash. R27 (old R28): 'clean' means reading only manifest inputs, the named user-level files included.

R1: one run lock, run/run.lock, for every shared write. It is created with wx and holds pid, start time and nonce. A busy lock gets a bounded retry, then exit 75. A stale lock is broken by rename and verified. Every ce and epoch check happens inside the lock, and temp files get unique names. The 'unparseable table' text is kept.

R2: the fence is a compare-and-set under the lock, and the staging cut is recorded at the fence (Kafka-style). The coordinator always passes the table's epoch. A stale READY is logged only as telemetry. Every script that writes takes --ce.

R3: now the step machine in the task row (fenced, stop-requested, stopped, admitted, started, bound). Reconcile runs every coordinator turn. Commit records and pack freezes are idempotent by exclusive create, and only owner messages keep an intent file.

R4: the watcher reads, decides and exits. It holds watcher.lock, checks ce first and again inside the lock, and spawns intake without waiting. Spend is computed by lib's parser. It exits at once on urgent events and within δ on others. A checker batch counts as an event only when full or blocking. There is no deadline exit.

R5: stall is now c calls with no fall in V, and hang is h ticks with no new call. The counters persist in run/watcher.json, a tick counts at most once per Δ, no wall clock is read, and a READY of the current epoch voids suspicion. Old R6 (pause detection) is deleted, and the N2 row now cites R5 (counters in calls and ticks).

R6 (old R7): endturn keeps two self-started wake sources (the watcher and the watch.mjs --alarm alarm) and writes acked_seq to coord.json under the lock. A coordinator with a stale ce writes nothing. The bound is restated in R6, the N3 row and R57, and the pilot injects one lost wake.

R7 (old R8): the checkpoint is the commit records plus staging prefixes up to the fence cut. Those objects enter in/ as untrusted and pass commit again. On a failure reason, replace first re-checks for a READY of the current epoch and refuses if it finds one. Hang is added to the causes. The layer 1 'assumptions fail' paragraph gets the new line-128 text and four more sentences.

R8 (old R9): R = 1 for any class. A reboot counts as class host (no charge to R or W_cc). On the limit path the order is fence, stop, then failed. The slot is freed only when the stop is confirmed. Memory parking counts toward H_max.
R9 (old R10): if a stop does not end the helpers, the owner ends the process, and its tokens are charged to B as zombie spend.

R10 (old R11): counts live processes, stop-unconfirmed ones included. The reservation is computed and never stored, and B is a target, not a bound. The gate is bound to the design-cut hash. Design-check tasks take slots, reservation and fencing but skip the gate. Gate A runs before reviews. 'Escrow' is renamed 'admission reservation' everywhere (§1, §2, R52, P8, P12, P14, G5, F4).

R11 (old R12): retitled 'Spend measured by script, stopped by the coordinator'. The 20 % meter halt is deleted, meter readings are logged as self-reported, overshoot is reported per incident with no bound, and a cut writes an overflow record whose ids stay visible.

R12 (old R13): the drain blocks every start, quiescence means no live child process of any epoch, and handover.mjs kills the watcher and the alarm and raises ce. The coordinator ends its turns at the 300k line if the owner does not answer. R50 (old R51) drops the 1.5·W* stop, and audit flags coordinator turns above 1.5·W*_coord. G8 'remains' now reads 'Obedience; only the owner can stop the coordinator'. §12 Coordinator hand-over lists options (a) drain (silent default), (b) crash-only and (c) the hand-over point, with the stated cost.js figures.

R28 (old R29): the reference is the commit hash in the owner's go, echoed and shown on the owner page, and the base is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof. fsck does the tcb check. R29 (old R30): user-level deny rules on the research paths, the canary also tests the denies, and audit exits 3 on writes to protected paths. replace writes folder settings. R31 (old R32): the tamper-evident wording replaces 'forward integrity'. R13 (old R14) and the role table: replace alone builds review-in/.

R32 (old R33): the harness validates against the child's schema, and harvest re-validates against tcb's card schema (altered schema leads to copied_by_session). R48(a) (old R49(a)) moves to later, and in the pilot the watcher logs predicted against realised t_q. §13 gets the hook-inputs unknown.

R21 (old R22): retitled 'Declared inputs'. The manifest includes the named user-level files and is the reference for R22 and R27. Keyed reuse and STALE-only repair move to later, and recovery is R7. The layer 2 'assumptions fail' paragraph is adjusted.

R35 (old R36): coverage is held-out seed recall with a Clopper-Pearson interval, labelled an upper bound by stated assumption. Chapman is pooled per field and only a diagnostic, and per-question two-route capture is later. R56 (old R57): the threshold and extra-lens rule are gone, and Chapman and Chao2 are readings. §8 now ends 'so the estimate is reported, not used as a stop', and §8 Borrowed whole calls the estimate a reading.

R42 (old R43): one seed per class per checker call, and the Clopper-Pearson bound counts calls (14 at d0 = 0.8). The fault list adds a lost wake and the §13 probes. R43 (old R44): the SPRT and the uncited lot are deleted (the lot moves to later), every cited card is checked, and the escape rate is reported. R44 (old R45): split into gate A (admit, R10) and the certificate. R45 (old R46) and §12 Thresholds: silence means the mapped default (d0 = 0.8, β = 0.05), and an item with no default is a reading.

R54 (old R55): gate.mjs --cut writes the design cut, and the blind analysts get only the cut in hermetic folders. Audit refuses an analysis that read the full design. They rerun when the cut hash changes. R55 (old R56): the gate binds to the hash of the cut plus hazards.jsonl, a tcb change reruns selftest and the canary only, and old R57 is no longer part of the gate. R57 (old R58): the model is the existing model.mjs, extended with the adopted designs and the strengthened properties. Its current verdict is recorded: blocked until the extended model holds.

R20 (old R21): render computes the seven measures (throughput, efficiency, token count, token cost with no currency, time taken, quality, hallucinations) for the owner page. Action lines and Comparison 1's secondaries are stated in them. §11 adds coordinator calls and tokens per field, owner interventions per hour and the owner's start latency.

§11: in Comparison 1, S1 runs with no fan-out to the 300k line, then stops (no compaction or hand-over), and its uncovered ids are counted. R53 (old R54) and F4 state the predicted total over every arm, marked stand-in. In Comparison 2 the child runs in amendment 1's form, judgment share is deleted, D8-07's uncited-sentence count is added, R2 is kept unconditionally and D6-10 is noted as an F2 option. In parameters, T_box becomes c and h; T_watch, pause detection, uncited-sample failures and certainty overturns are removed.

§12: F1 has options (a) amendment 1 (silent default) and (b) fresh, with the fresh path running at least once per wave; the pilot writes both reviews and the owner rules after. F2's silent default is no second expert, with the options listed. A new item covers the research child's window: (a) amendment 1 (default), (b) roll-overs. The hand-over measure gains 'quality'. The hook item states each option's reach.

R46-R48 (old R47-R49): in the pilot the leaves are the lanes, with one capacity check at pack freeze, and plan-tree runs after the pilot on measured t_q. R48 is pilot only for (b) and (e). (d) becomes a later split with a separator in tree-plan.json, and the synthesis gate on unresolved ranges is later. R49 (old R50) applies only under option (b) of the research child's window.

§9 rows updated as the edit lists (P8, P9, P10, P11, P12, P13, N2, N3, N5, N7, N9, N16, G8). For consistency, P15 (refuter later), P16 (held-out seed recall), P19 (c calls), S (lanes in the pilot), G4 and G5 are also updated, and every Rules cell is renumbered.

§10: replaced by the final pilot set (25 scripts plus lib.mjs, the merges, the files), the moved-to-later list, the deleted-not-deferred list, and 'Left out on purpose'. That last list no longer repeats the B+ parts and points to §7 instead. The Scripts lines in §2-§8 are updated to the merged set, and §13 Size now reads '25 small scripts and the shared library lib.mjs'.

§13: adds the six unverified harness facts (OS processes, process start time via PowerShell, background-exit wakes, binding user-level denies, which settings apply, hook inputs), each with a probe in R42 and the fallback.

Rules renumbered after deleting old R6: every rule from old R7 on moved down by one (R7 became R6 ... R59 became R58), and all references in the rules, the §9 table and the pilot and later lists were fixed by script (224 references). 'Reading it' now says R1 to R58. Arm names R1 and R2 and R_same are unaffected.

Final-pass fixes: the rule that had lost its runner is now covered: R46 key-space check, by protocol-freeze (plan-tree repeats it later). R21 gets [replace, audit]. Sources with no remaining user were removed: Gordon/Milner/Wadsworth from row 3 and §14; Wald and 'sequential tests' from row 5 and §14, since the SPRT is deleted. tcb.lock.json references are gone from R10, R41 and R55. The coordinator's Agent list drops the refuter. In R54, the refuter's sampling of 'n/a' cells is marked later. In R11, 'Cutting a task writes' avoids a third meaning of 'the cut'. R12 names coord.json as state.

not_applied.why: The list names 26 .mjs files including lib.mjs. I kept 25 by counting lib.mjs separately as 'the shared library', in both §10 and §13 Size. Change it if 26 was meant.

Taken literally, the replacement drops the definitions of W_cc and H_max, which the new text itself uses ('no count toward W_cc', 'counts toward H_max'). I kept 'Planned replacements do not count toward R; hand-overs stop at H_max; two failures within W_cc halt admission' and dropped only the split (R49 is later), 'slot freed' (replaced by the stop-confirmed rule) and 'unspent escrow released' (no stored escrow).

not_applied.edit: §10 'Remove the refuter brief from the pilot'
not_applied.why: R54 (old R55) still had a refuter sample the FMEA 'n/a' cells. With no refuter brief in the pilot I marked that sampling 'Later' rather than leave a rule with no runner. It is not in the edit's moved-to-later list.
Its runner was plan-tree, which moved to later. To keep a pilot runner I named protocol-freeze, which already freezes the question ids. This choice is not in the edits.

not_applied.edit: §9 P13 'replace SPRT with gate A, certificate'
not_applied.why: A literal replacement would repeat 'certificate' beside 'Script certificate'. The cell now reads 'Script certificate, plants, gate A, read-set hash'.

Old R6 was deleted, so rules from R7 on were renumbered as the task asks. Rule numbers in the edits JSON, earlier reviews, the model README and other documents now point one higher than this file. No note about this was added to the document, because the edits do not ask for one.
